h: Building Confidence One Obstacle at a Time
p: Obstacle courses are brilliant for building resilience. Children quickly learn that falling off isn't the end of the world, and that if they keep trying, they'll get further each time. For kids who lack confidence in sport, a place like this can be a great leveller, because nobody expects you to be perfect.

Parents can help by focusing on effort rather than results. Cheer the attempt, not just the success, and you'll find even nervous children start to give things a go. Some kids might want to stick to the easier obstacles at first, and that's absolutely fine.

Walsall has a few gems to round off the day. The Walsall Leather Museum tells the story of the town's famous saddle and leather trade, with workshops and displays that are surprisingly interesting. Barr Beacon, a high point just outside the town, has views stretching for miles on a clear day and is a great spot for a short walk and a picnic.

The Birmingham Canal Navigations run through the area too, so a towpath stroll is easy to fit in. Walsall's location also makes it handy for families travelling from across the Black Country and Staffordshire. Arrive a few minutes early, get shoes and coats sorted, and let the kids watch a run or two before they start. It helps settle the nerves before their first go.
